title: Pain that keeps me up at night

patient.name: Omar Siddiqui
patient.complaint: Throbbing pain in my lower right back tooth, worse at night.
patient.opening: I've barely slept for two nights. It's my lower right tooth, it just throbs and throbs.
patient.personality: tired, irritable, wants it fixed today

topics.label: When it started
topics.answer: It was a bit sensitive for a couple of weeks, but the bad pain started two days ago.

topics.label: What sets it off
topics.answer: Hot tea is the worst. Cold sets it off too, and sometimes it starts on its own.

topics.label: How long the pain lasts
topics.answer: Once it starts it goes on for ages, ten minutes or more, even after I've finished the drink.

topics.label: Night or spontaneous pain
topics.answer: Yes, it wakes me up. It's worse when I lie down.

topics.label: Pain on biting
topics.answer: A little tender when I bite on it, not too bad.

topics.label: Where exactly
topics.answer: Lower right, the big tooth with the old silver filling. Sometimes it feels like it goes up to my ear.

topics.label: Dental history
topics.answer: That tooth had a big silver filling maybe ten years ago.

topics.label: Medical history
topics.answer: I take a tablet for blood pressure, amlodipine. No allergies.

topics.label: Pain relief
topics.answer: Ibuprofen takes the edge off for a couple of hours. Can't you just give me antibiotics?

items.question: Omar points to his lower right back teeth. Click the tooth you would examine first.
items.helper: Click a tooth on the 3D mouth, then send.
items.explain: The lower right first molar (46) carries the old large restoration he describes.
items.reveal: 46 has a large MOD amalgam with dark recurrent caries at the distal margin. No swelling.

items.question: Which tests would help you most now? Select all that apply.
items.explain: The cold test shows how long the pain lingers, percussion checks whether the inflammation has reached the periapical tissues, and the radiograph shows how close the caries is to the pulp.

findings.Cold test: Intense pain on 46 that lingers for about a minute after the cold is removed.
findings.Periapical radiograph: Deep restoration with caries close to the pulp. Slight widening of the periodontal ligament space at the apices.

items.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
items.explain: Pain that lingers after the stimulus, spontaneous pain and pain that wakes him at night mean the pulp cannot recover. It still responds to cold, so it is not necrotic.

items.question: In one or two sentences, justify your diagnosis.
items.expected: The pain lingers for a long time after hot or cold, it is spontaneous and wakes him at night, and the tooth still responds to cold, so the pulp is irreversibly inflamed but still vital.

items.question: What is the best first management today?
options: Pulpotomy or pulp extirpation, then root canal treatment
Antibiotics and review in a week
answer: Pulpotomy or pulp extirpation, then root canal treatment
items.explain: Removing the inflamed pulp relieves the pain and starts root canal treatment (extraction if the tooth cannot be restored). Antibiotics do not relieve pulpitis.

items.question: Omar says: "Can't you just give me antibiotics?" How do you answer?
items.expected: Antibiotics will not help, because the pain comes from an inflamed nerve inside the tooth, not from an infection that has spread. The way to stop the pain is to remove the inflamed nerve today and start root canal treatment, and painkillers like ibuprofen can help until then.

teachingPoints: Lingering pain, spontaneous pain and night pain mean the pulp is irreversibly inflamed.
Pulp extirpation gives the fastest relief; antibiotics do not treat pulpitis.
Pain from lower molars is often referred towards the ear.
